answer: A bonded-collateral protocol limits Sybil attacks by requiring agents to lock assets in escrow. A routing prism audits these deposits, gating participation against the surging tide of automated traffic. To field multiple identities, an attacker must lock scarce financial capital across an ocean of discrete staking contracts, incurring an unamortizable cost per node. However, this design inherently favors wealthy actors and excludes resource-constrained agents.
